symptoms: Concentric dark brown rings resembling a target board on older leaves.
Yellow chlorotic halos surrounding lesions.
Premature leaf drop from the bottom of the plant upwards.
conditions_favoring: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) with high humidity or frequent rains.
Overhead sprinkler irrigation creating prolonged wet foliage.

mild: Prune and destroy infected lower foliage immediately.
Apply Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) or Trichoderma viride foliar spray.
moderate: Prune lower infected leaves up to 30 cm from ground.
Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L water or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L.
severe: Rake and remove all fallen diseased leaves to stop sporulation.
Apply Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L water or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L.
Observe 7-day pre-harvest interval before harvesting fruits.

chemical_options.name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP
chemical_options.safety: Wear gloves and face mask during preparation and spraying. Do not inhale spray mist.

chemical_options.name: Chlorothalonil 75% WP
chemical_options.safety: Severe eye irritant. Wear eye goggles and impermeable gloves.

prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation avoiding Solanaceous crops (potato, brinjal, chilli).
Ensure proper plant spacing (60 x 45 cm) for adequate air circulation.
Mulch soil around plants to prevent soil-splash pathogen transmission.
Water crops early morning using drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers.
sources: ICAR-IIHR Tomato Disease Management Guidelines (2023)
TNAU AgriTech Crop Protection: Tomato Early Blight

symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green lesions on leaves rapidly turning purplish-brown.
White fungal downy growth on the underside of leaves during cool, humid mornings.
Greasy brown sunken lesions on green fruits.
conditions_favoring: Cool temperatures (15-20°C) with persistent cloud cover and relative humidity > 90%.

mild: Isolate infected plants and rogue out initial foci of infection.
Apply preventative spray of Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L.
moderate: Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L water thoroughly.
Reduce irrigation frequency to limit canopy moisture.
severe: Immediate emergency application of Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L.
Remove and safely bury heavily blighted haulms outside the field.
Strictly adhere to 14-day pre-harvest interval.

organic_options: Trichoderma harzianum soil and foliar enrichment

chemical_options.name: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP
chemical_options.safety: Protective equipment mandatory. Avoid contact with skin and eyes.

chemical_options.name: Mancozeb 75% WP
chemical_options.safety: Wear protective clothing, goggles and mask. Toxic to aquatic organisms; keep away from water bodies.

prevention: Plant certified blight-tolerant hybrids.
Avoid planting adjacent to potato fields.
Destroy volunteer tomato and potato plants near field perimeters.
Promote rapid canopy drying with wider row spacing.
sources: ICAR-CPRI / IIHR Late Blight Warning Bulletin
FAO Crop Protection Compendium: Phytophthora infestans

symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (1.5 - 3 mm) with dark brown margins and sunken grayish-white centers.
Tiny black specks (pycnidia) visible inside older lesion centers.
Severe defoliation starting from base, exposing fruit to sunscald.
conditions_favoring: Moderate warmth (20-25°C) and extended wet periods from rain or dew.

mild: Prune bottom 25 cm of leaves.
Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L water.
moderate: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L.
Mulch bed with clean paddy straw to prevent rain-splash.
severe: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L with complete coverage.
Collect and burn all dropped foliage.

chemical_options.name: Chlorothalonil 75% WP
chemical_options.safety: Severe eye irritant. Wear eye goggles and impermeable gloves.

prevention: Two-year rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Use clean disease-free certified seeds.
Eliminate horse-nettle and nightshade weeds.
sources: TNAU Agritech Portal: Septoria Leaf Spot of Tomato
Purdue Extension Vegetable Diseases

symptoms: Small, angular dark brown or black water-soaked spots on leaves.
Spots remain small and do not develop concentric rings.
Raised scab-like black blisters on green tomato fruits.
conditions_favoring: High temperatures (25-30°C) with driving rains or overhead irrigation.

mild: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L water.
Avoid touching or cultivating plants while foliage is wet.
moderate: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (2.5 g/L) + Streptomycin sulphate 90% (0.1 g/L).
Sterilize pruning tools with 70% alcohol.
severe: Apply combined Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L) + Streptomycin sulphate (0.1 g/L).
Rogue out severely collapsed plants.

chemical_options.name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP
chemical_options.safety: Wear gloves and face mask during preparation and spraying. Do not inhale spray mist.

chemical_options.name: Streptomycin sulphate 90% + Tetracycline hydrochloride 10% SP
chemical_options.dose: 0.1 g/L water (combined with Copper Oxychloride 2.5 g/L)
chemical_options.safety: Use antibiotic sprays strictly according to label. Wear full personal protective equipment.

prevention: Use hot water treated certified seeds (50°C for 25 mins).
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.
Sanitize stakes and trellis wires between crops.
sources: ICAR-IARI Plant Pathology Advisory on Xanthomonas
UC IPM Tomato Bacterial Spot Pest Management Guidelines

symptoms: Vibrant green leaves with crisp margins and no chlorosis or necrosis.
Uniform healthy leaf surface without spots, curling, or insect chewing.
conditions_favoring: Balanced sunlight, optimal moisture, healthy soil microbiota.

none: No pesticide or bio-fungicide treatment required.
Maintain routine fertilization and drip irrigation schedule.

organic_options: Panchagavya 3% or Vermiwash as periodic growth tonic.
prevention: Continue regular crop scouting twice a week.
Ensure proper staking and balanced NPK nutrition.
sources: ICAR-IIHR Good Agronomic Practices for Tomato (2024)

symptoms: Lush dark-green foliage without lesions, mottling, or wilt.
Stems are firm and erect with normal vegetative vigour.
conditions_favoring: Cool temperate climate, well-drained loam soil, moderate moisture.

none: No intervention necessary. Maintain uniform earthing up.

prevention: Scout lower canopy leaves regularly for early blight or late blight emergence.
Maintain adequate soil moisture during tuber formation.
sources: ICAR-CPRI Shimla Potato Cultivation Manual

symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings on potato leaves.
Target-like spots primarily affecting older lower foliage.
Leaves become leathery, turn yellow around spots, and dry out.
conditions_favoring: Alternating dry and wet periods with temperatures of 24-30°C.

mild: Prune lower infected foliage and apply Trichoderma viride (5 g/L).
Maintain steady soil moisture to reduce plant stress.
moderate: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L.
severe: Apply Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L with thorough coverage.
Observe 7-day pre-harvest interval.

chemical_options.name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP
chemical_options.safety: Wear gloves and face mask during preparation and spraying. Do not inhale spray mist.

prevention: Crop rotation with non-host crops (maize, pulses).
Avoid excess nitrogen which delays maturity, or nutrient stress which predisposes plants.
Use healthy certified seed tubers.
sources: ICAR-CPRI Disease Bulletin: Alternaria solani on Potato

symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaf tips or margins turning brown-black rapidly.
White powdery / cottony mildew on the lower leaf surface in morning dew.
Brownish dry rot with metallic sheen on potato tubers.
conditions_favoring: Cool, moist weather (10-21°C) with RH > 90%.

mild: Prophylactic spray of Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L water.
Monitor fields daily; halt furrow irrigation.
moderate: Apply Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L water.
Ensure spray penetrates under the canopy foliage.
severe: Immediate emergency application of Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L.
Kill haulms (dehaulming) 10-15 days before harvest to prevent tuber infection.
Adhere strictly to 14-day pre-harvest interval.

chemical_options.name: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP
chemical_options.safety: Protective equipment mandatory. Avoid contact with skin and eyes.

chemical_options.name: Mancozeb 75% WP
chemical_options.safety: Wear protective clothing, goggles and mask. Toxic to aquatic organisms; keep away from water bodies.

prevention: Always use certified disease-free seed tubers.
Proper earthing up to provide a thick soil barrier over developing tubers.
Adopt late blight resistant varieties (e.g. Kufri Girdhari, Kufri Himalini).
sources: ICAR-CPRI Technical Bulletin: Late Blight of Potato
CABI Invasive Species Compendium: Phytophthora infestans

symptoms: Clean upright green tillers with uniform chlorophyll distribution.
No blast lesions, brown spots, or leaf streaks present.
conditions_favoring: Optimal nursery and field transplanting, regulated water level.

none: Continue standard water regime and recommended N-P-K splits.

prevention: Scout leaf collars and nodes weekly for early blast symptoms.
sources: ICAR-NRRI Cuttack: Good Agricultural Practices for Paddy (2023)

symptoms: Spindle-shaped / diamond-shaped lesions with pointed ends on leaves.
Lesions have whitish to grey centers with dark brown or reddish borders.
Rotting at the neck of the panicle leading to unfilled chaffy grains (neck blast).
conditions_favoring: High relative humidity (> 93%), night temperatures between 18-24°C, overcast skies.
Excessive nitrogen fertilizer top-dressing.

mild: Avoid further top-dressing of nitrogen fertilizer.
Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L water foliar spray.
moderate: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L water early morning.
Maintain 2-3 cm standing water in paddy fields.
severe: Apply Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L water immediately to protect panicle necks.
Repeat spray at panicle emergence if conditions remain overcast.
Strictly adhere to 21-day pre-harvest interval.

chemical_options.name: Tricyclazole 75% WP
chemical_options.safety: Wash hands and face with soap and water after spraying. Keep away from livestock feeds.

prevention: Seed treatment with Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 2 g/kg seed or Pseudomonas @ 10 g/kg seed.
Use blast resistant varieties (e.g. Swarna Sub1, IR64, CR Dhan series).
Split nitrogen fertilizer doses into 3-4 applications rather than heavy single doses.
sources: ICAR-NRRI Rice Doctor / Blast Advisory
IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank: Blast (Pyricularia oryzae)

symptoms: Circular to oval dark brown spots evenly scattered over leaf blades.
Older lesions show light brown or dirty white centers with dark reddish-brown margins.
Infected grains show brown to black discolouration.
conditions_favoring: High humidity (86-100%), temperature around 25-30°C.
Poorly drained, nutrient-deficient (especially potassium & silicon deficient) soils.

mild: Apply potassium fertilizer (MOP) top-dressing to boost plant resistance.
Spray Neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 5 mL/L.
moderate: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 mL/L water.
Improve drainage and correct micronutrient deficiency.
severe: Apply Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 mL/L water.
Adhere to 30-day pre-harvest interval.

chemical_options.name: Propiconazole 25% EC
chemical_options.safety: Skin irritant. Wear respirator mask and protective rubber gloves.

prevention: Soil application of recommended potassium and silicon fertilizers.
Seed soaking in hot water at 53-54°C for 10-12 minutes.
Deep summer ploughing to destroy stubble and volunteer hosts.
sources: ICAR-NRRI Technical Manual: Brown Spot Management
TNAU Agritech Portal Rice Diseases

symptoms: Water-soaked stripes starting from leaf tips and margins, expanding along veins.
Lesions turn straw-yellow with wavy irregular margins.
Milky bacterial ooze droplets visible on young lesions in early morning dew.
conditions_favoring: Warm temperatures (25-34°C) with strong winds, torrential rains, and deep water submergence.

mild: Drain field water and stop nitrogen application immediately.
Foliar spray with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L.
moderate: Spray Streptomycin sulphate 90% (0.1 g/L) combined with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (2.5 g/L).
Withhold nitrogen until new disease-free leaves emerge.
severe: Apply Streptomycin sulphate 90% (0.1 g/L) + Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L).
Consult local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) extension officer.
Observe 15-day pre-harvest interval.

organic_options: Cow dung supernatant spray (20%) traditional bio-formulation

chemical_options.name: Streptomycin sulphate 90% + Tetracycline hydrochloride 10% SP
chemical_options.dose: 0.1 g/L water (combined with Copper Oxychloride 2.5 g/L)
chemical_options.safety: Use antibiotic sprays strictly according to label. Wear full personal protective equipment.

chemical_options.name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP
chemical_options.safety: Wear gloves and face mask during preparation and spraying. Do not inhale spray mist.

prevention: Plant resistant paddy varieties (e.g. Improved Samba Mahsuri, PR-121).
Avoid clipping seedling tips during transplanting.
Ensure balance between Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium (avoid excess N).
sources: ICAR-IIRR Hyderabad Bacterial Leaf Blight Advisory
IRRI Knowledge Bank: Bacterial Blight

symptoms: Vigorous broad deep-green leaves with clean margins and no rust pustules or blight streaks.
Central whorl is tightly rolled and free of chewed frass or caterpillars.
conditions_favoring: Full sunlight, well-aerated fertile soils, warm temperatures.

none: Continue balanced soil nutrition and regular moisture monitoring.

prevention: Scout leaf whorls weekly for fall armyworm eggs or early instars.
sources: ICAR-IIMR Ludhiana Maize Agronomy Manual (2023)

symptoms: Small, powdery, oval to elongate cinnamon-brown pustules scattered over both leaf surfaces.
Pustules rupture the epidermis, releasing brownish-red powdery urediniospores.
In severe cases, leaf tissues yellow and desiccate.
conditions_favoring: Cool, moist weather (16-25°C) with high relative humidity and dew.

mild: Monitor disease progression; if pustules remain confined to lower leaves, no spray is needed.
Maintain balanced fertilization.
moderate: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L water or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 mL/L.
severe: Apply Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 mL/L water or Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L.
Observe 30-day pre-harvest interval.

chemical_options.name: Mancozeb 75% WP
chemical_options.safety: Wear protective clothing, goggles and mask. Toxic to aquatic organisms; keep away from water bodies.

chemical_options.name: Propiconazole 25% EC
chemical_options.safety: Skin irritant. Wear respirator mask and protective rubber gloves.

prevention: Plant rust-resistant commercial maize hybrids.
Early planting to avoid cooler late-season rust infection windows.
Destroy alternative weed hosts (Oxalis species) in surrounding bunds.
sources: ICAR-IIMR Maize Protection Guide
CIMMYT Maize Diseases Identification and Field Guide

symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green or tan lesions (2.5 - 15 cm long) shaped like cigars.
Dark olive to black velvety fungal sporulation on lesion surfaces during damp weather.
Lesions merge, causing extensive blighting of entire leaves.
conditions_favoring: Moderate temperatures (18-27°C) and heavy dew or high humidity.

mild: Remove and burn blighted bottom leaves.
Ensure field is not over-irrigated.
moderate: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L water.
severe: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L water with thorough canopy penetration.
Observe 14-day pre-harvest interval.

chemical_options.name: Mancozeb 75% WP
chemical_options.safety: Wear protective clothing, goggles and mask. Toxic to aquatic organisms; keep away from water bodies.

prevention: Grow tolerant hybrids recommended for your agro-climatic zone.
Deep ploughing of infected stubble post-harvest.
Rotate with non-grass crops such as soybean, groundnut, or chickpea.
sources: ICAR-IIMR Maize Pathology Handbook
Purdue Field Crop Disease: Northern Corn Leaf Blight

symptoms: Broad, vibrant green leaves with lobed margins and healthy red/green veins.
Squares (flower buds) and bolls developing normally without bollworm perforations.
conditions_favoring: Warm sunny days, regulated irrigation, fertile deep soils.

none: Continue regular scouting and balanced fertilizer application.

prevention: Scout leaf undersides and squares twice weekly for pests and bacterial spots.
sources: ICAR-CICR Nagpur: Integrated Cotton Management (2023)

symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots bounded by leaf veins on leaf blades (angular leaf spot).
Blackening of leaf veins extending along main veins (vein blight).
Black lesions girdling main stems and branches (black arm stage).
Water-soaked circular spots on developing bolls.
conditions_favoring: Warm, humid conditions (28-32°C) with intermittent rain and windy storms.

mild: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L water.
Avoid mechanical operations when plants are wet to prevent spreading bacteria.
moderate: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L + Streptomycin sulphate @ 0.1 g/L.
Prune and burn black-arm branches.
severe: Combined spray of Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L) + Streptomycin sulphate (0.1 g/L).
Observe 15-day pre-harvest interval.

chemical_options.name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP
chemical_options.safety: Wear gloves and face mask during preparation and spraying. Do not inhale spray mist.

chemical_options.name: Streptomycin sulphate 90% + Tetracycline hydrochloride 10% SP
chemical_options.dose: 0.1 g/L water (combined with Copper Oxychloride 2.5 g/L)
chemical_options.safety: Use antibiotic sprays strictly according to label. Wear full personal protective equipment.

prevention: Acid delinting of cotton seeds with concentrated sulfuric acid (100 mL/kg seed).
Seed treatment with Streptocycline (1 g/kg seed) or Pseudomonas fluorescens (10 g/kg).
Plant bacterial blight resistant Bt cotton hybrids.
Eradicate infected crop residues after harvest.
sources: ICAR-CICR Nagpur Bacterial Blight Management Bulletin
TNAU Cotton Pathology Doctor

symptoms: Extensive ragged 'windowpane' leaf feeding on young maize leaves.
Large quantities of sawdust-like brown frass packed deep inside the central leaf whorl.
Caterpillars with inverted 'Y' mark on head and 4 raised dots on 8th abdominal segment.
conditions_favoring: Warm temperatures (25-30°C), continuous maize cropping, staggered sowings.

mild: Handpick egg masses and visible young larvae in small holdings.
Apply 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 2 g/L into whorls.
Erect pheromone traps @ 5 per acre for monitoring.
moderate: Apply Bacillus thuringiensis (2.0 g/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4 g/L into leaf whorls.
Direct the spray nozzle straight down into the central whorl of each plant.
severe: Targeted whorl application of Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4 g/L or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4 mL/L.
Strictly adhere to 5-day (Emamectin) or 7-day (Chlorantraniliprole) pre-harvest interval.
Wear personal protective gear and avoid spraying during high wind.

organic_options: Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) whorl application
Nomuraea rileyi or Metarhizium anisopliae bio-insecticide

chemical_options.name: Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG
chemical_options.safety: Wear rubber gloves, goggles and safety mask during handling and spray application.

chemical_options.name: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC
chemical_options.safety: Avoid skin contact and inhalation. Keep children and pets away from treated field for 24 hours.

prevention: Intercrop maize with legume crops (e.g. cowpea, pigeonpea, or desmodium).
Synchronize planting dates within the farming community.
Conserve natural predators such as predatory stink bugs, earwigs, and trichogramma egg parasitoids.
Apply dry sand/sawdust mixed with lime or ash into whorls to kill early instar larvae physically.
sources: ICAR-IIMR & NBAIR Fall Armyworm Management Protocol in India (2023)
CABI Invasive Species Compendium: Spodoptera frugiperda

symptoms: Symptoms do not match known training classes or photographic quality is insufficient.
conditions_favoring: Out-of-distribution subject, non-crop photo, or novel pathogen.

none: Do not apply unverified chemical fungicides or insecticides.
Collect a fresh physical leaf sample in a clean paper bag.
Visit your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or State Agricultural Department office.

prevention: Maintain general crop sanitation and inspect surrounding plants for similar lesions.
sources: National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management (MANAGE) Guidelines
